perspective:
**Ethan’s available information, from his own perspective:**

- I am Ethan Mohamud, a plumber. Gary Guo is my long-time friend; we met in middle school. He is a doctor.
- I noticed Gary was working extremely long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. I became concerned about his health.
- I invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation. I told him his health was just as important and that it might give him a new perspective.
- Gary told me he appreciated my concern but said he couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, I observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected there was more going on than just professional obligations.
- I confronted Gary, reminding him we’ve been friends since middle school, that he can tell me anything, and that I was there to help, not judge.
- Gary told me it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden me with his problems.
- After that, Gary opened up to me about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. I felt relief and empathy.
- I offered to help him find a better balance, suggesting he prioritize tasks and delegate some responsibilities.
- Gary told me that sounded good and that he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself too.
- Over the following months, I checked in with Gary regularly, discussed his progress and remaining challenges, saw him making efforts, and felt hopeful and proud. I continued encouraging him.
- Gary told me things were better, that thanks to my help he wasn’t as overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- I told him I was proud of his progress and that I was there whenever he needed to talk.
- After about a year, I saw Gary managing on his own and felt satisfied and happy for him. I decided it was time to step back but let him know I’d always be a call away.
- Gary told me he couldn’t have done it without my support and that he felt more in control now.

I have no access to Gary’s private thoughts or events I did not personally observe, hear, or get told by Gary.
